title: NEB Class 12 Physics — Communication Systems — 2024
subject: physics
source: NEB Grade 12 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: What is modulation? Distinguish between amplitude modulation and frequency modulation, and state one advantage of FM over AM.
questions.solution:
**Modulation** is the process of superimposing a low-frequency message signal on a high-frequency carrier wave so the signal can be radiated over long distances by an antenna of practical size.

**AM:** the amplitude of the carrier varies with the message; the sideband bandwidth is 2f_m, and noise affects amplitude strongly.

**FM:** the frequency varies with the message; bandwidth ≈ 2(f_m + Δf), which is wider.

**Advantage of FM:** noise immunity — amplitude noise (lightning, sparks) can be clipped away, so reception is much clearer.
questions.knowledgeNote: Antenna length must be comparable to λ/4, which is why audio (≈20 Hz–20 kHz) cannot be radiated directly and needs a carrier in the MHz range.

questions.question: Explain the terms ground wave, sky wave and space wave propagation with one suitable use of each.
questions.solution:
**Ground wave:** the wave travels along the Earth's surface; useful for medium-wave broadcast over short ranges, attenuated as frequency rises.

**Sky wave:** the wave is refracted back by the ionosphere and can travel thousands of kilometres; used for short-wave radio, but is unstable as ionisation changes with time of day.

**Space wave:** line-of-sight propagation direct from transmitter to receiver (plus a ground-reflected component); used for VHF/UHF TV, radar and satellite links, with range limited by the horizon.
questions.knowledgeNote: Satellite communication uses space waves above ~30 MHz, where the ionosphere no longer reflects the signal.

questions.question: Define bandwidth of a signal and calculate the bandwidth needed if a message of 5 kHz is transmitted by (a) AM and (b) FM with a frequency deviation of 20 kHz.
questions.solution:
**Bandwidth** is the range of frequencies a signal occupies.

**(a) AM:** 2f_m = 2 × 5 = **10 kHz**.

**(b) FM:** 2(f_m + Δf) = 2(5 + 20) = **50 kHz**, using Carson's rule.
questions.knowledgeNote: FM needs a wider channel than AM but trades bandwidth for noise immunity — a recurring NEB comparison.
